colormaps.name: turbo
colormaps.note: Google polynomial approximation; one shared p range for CFD and PINO.

colormaps.name: diverging
colormaps.note: Moreland cool-warm; symmetric about zero; values past +absMax take the over color.

colormaps.name: viridis
colormaps.note: Degree-6 polynomial fit of matplotlib viridis.

display.purpose: Hero headline only; Archivo width 92, max 15ch.

display-page.purpose: h1 of the report surfaces (publications, record, cv); max 20ch.

body.purpose: Reading column, ledes, role line; 60ch measure.

caption.purpose: Figure and table captions, viewer notes, status lines; italic STIX in ink-2.

ui.purpose: Nav, buttons, footer links, anchors, summaries.

mono.purpose: Result lines, citations, DOIs, readouts, BibTeX; tabular numerals.

label.purpose: Corner chrome, colorbar labels, tags, axis labels; uppercase only for short unit-free identifiers.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system is flat. Separation is a 1px hairline in --line or a one-step tonal lift to --bg-1.

shadows.name: segment-pressed-underline
shadows.purpose: A 2px signal underline on a pressed segmented button, drawn as an inset box-shadow. An underline, not an elevation.

texture.name: film-grain
texture.value: feTurbulence fractalNoise baseFrequency 0.9, 2 octaves, desaturated, 256px tile, opacity 0.05, position fixed, z-index 2147483000
texture.purpose: One static grain sheet over film surfaces via body::after; never animated; removed in print.

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: State transitions: hover color, border, underline, skip link.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Reserved slow step; declared, not yet consumed by a component.

motion.name: duration-develop
motion.purpose: The PINO layer develops over the CFD field for the measured inference time (1.78 s on one L40S) while the readout counts; snaps under reduced motion.

motion.name: drift-period
motion.purpose: Idle C-arm drift of the vessel, one revolution; paused offscreen and on document.hidden; 0s under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for every transition.

breakpoints.name: nav-ghost-drop
breakpoints.purpose: The ghost CV (PDF) nav action drops; Email stays.

breakpoints.name: about-one
breakpoints.purpose: About collapses to one column; portrait 7rem.

breakpoints.name: pulse-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Spectrogram axis column 2.25rem, tighter plot padding.

breakpoints.name: pub-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Publication plate and row stack to one column.

breakpoints.name: nav-menu
breakpoints.purpose: The four page links fold into the inline Menu disclosure; actions stay in the 3rem row.

breakpoints.name: hero-portrait
breakpoints.purpose: Hero frame goes 3/4 portrait, headline moves below, wipe becomes a two-state toggle.

breakpoints.name: close-split
breakpoints.purpose: Close becomes two columns: text and a 32rem action column.

breakpoints.name: fronts-single
breakpoints.purpose: Three Fronts strip collapses to one column; Flow frame 4/3.

breakpoints.name: about-two
breakpoints.purpose: About drops to two columns, photo under the text; portrait 8rem.

breakpoints.name: frame-width
breakpoints.purpose: Max width of the frame column.

layout.widthText: 1280px (same box as the frame column; text narrows by measure only)
layout.widthTextDeclaredUnused: 72rem (--width-text in tokens.css, no container reads it)
layout.leftEdge: One left edge: every column starts where the frames, nav and footer start.

formatting.unitJoin: U+202F narrow no-break space between value and unit and as thousands separator (8 649)
formatting.range: en dash, one trailing unit (10.7–13.0 kPa)

precision.quantity: FFR Pd/Pa (metrics table case column; CFD-PINO difference)

formatting.manuscriptStatus: under revision (EAAI): lowercase, venue short form, printed once per entry (year corner on Led and /publications; venue line with abbr on /research PaperFrame)
formatting.doi: doi:<identifier>, lowercase, no space, mono, linked to https://doi.org/
formatting.proseCounts: numberWord: counts in ledes spelled as words
formatting.voice: First person for copy that speaks for the owner (About, Close, my-part lines); third person for author lists and collaborators.

} .ds-scrub-grip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal, oklch(0.62 0.21 27)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-scrub-readout { margin: 0; font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--bone-2, oklch(0.74 0.012 85)); components.name: Paper Plate

components.css: .ds-plate { display: grid; gap: 1rem; width: 100%; max-width: 35rem; margin: 0; padding: 1rem; background: var(--film-0, oklch(0.15 0.008 250)); } .ds-plate-sheet { display: block; padding: 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--film-line, oklch(0.38 0.01 250)); border-radius: 2px; background: var(--box, oklch(0.975 0.004 85)); cursor: zoom-in; } .ds-plate-sheet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal, oklch(0.62 0.21 27)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-plate-raster { display: block; aspect-ratio: 1855 / 728; background: linear-gradient(transparent 49%, var(--box-line, oklch(0.86 0.012 250)) 49%, var(--box-line, oklch(0.86 0.012 250)) 51%, transparent 51%); mix-blend-mode: multiply; } .ds-plate-caption { max-width: 62ch; font-family: 'STIX Two Text', 'Times New Roman', Georgia, serif; font-style: italic; font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--bone-2, oklch(0.74 0.012 85)); }

narrative.overview:
The site is a cath-lab cine frame and the research is the image inside it. Every surface is read the way a cardiologist reads a run: a hairline-bordered frame, mono readouts pinned in the corners, the data filling the middle, and a fixed caption beneath it saying what it is, what it measured, and what follows. Nothing decorative competes with the vessel, the FFR curve or the spectrogram; UI chrome is thin, mono and tinted so it reads as instrument markings rather than interface.

Two surfaces share one ink and one accent. The data surfaces (/, /research) sit on film charcoal: a cool near-black that is never pure, under a single static grain sheet. The report surfaces (/publications, /record, /cv) sit on light-box white with the same bone-tinted ink family inverted and the same clinical red. Components never read the raw film or box values; they read semantic aliases (--bg, --ink, --line) that the <html data-surface> attribute resolves, so one component works unchanged on both surfaces.

Rank is carried by border ink and by frame size, never by weight, fill or color flooding. First-author work gets the larger frame and the signal-red border on its role mark; co-authored work gets a compact ruled row and a hairline. Type weight stays even across the hierarchy (one display weight, 600) so the eye ranks by geometry, not by shouting.
keyCharacteristics: Film charcoal and light-box white as two surfaces of one world; identical ink roles and one red on both.
Frame, not card: hairline border, 2px radius, mono corner chrome, three-tier caption stack (what / result / consequence).
Three faces with fixed jobs: Archivo (width 92) for display and UI, STIX Two Text for reading, JetBrains Mono for every number, unit, identifier and readout.
Flat throughout; depth is a hairline, a tonal step or a fixed grain, never a shadow or gradient.
Signal red is reserved: probes, the PINO trace, active underlines, focus rings, selection and the one primary action per page.
Motion is physical evidence: the PINO layer develops over the measured 1.78 s, the vessel drifts one revolution per 60 s, and both stop under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Each surface has exactly one ink family (bone on film, box-ink on light box) in three tiers, plus the one signal red. No other UI color exists; colormaps belong to the data, not the chrome.

rules.name: The Alias Rule
rules.body: Components read --bg, --bg-1, --bg-2, --line, --line-soft, --ink, --ink-2, --ink-3 only. Raw film-* and box-* values are set once per surface in tokens.css and referenced directly only when an element must hold the opposite surface inside a frame (the paper plate).

rules.name: The Light-Box Rule
rules.body: White inside a film frame is the light box of the world, never a bare rectangle: it carries a 1px hairline and mono corner chrome or a caption, and holds only a raster that came from the paper or the data. Paper rasters on the light box are composited with mix-blend-mode: multiply, so the figure's own white becomes the box ground instead of a second rectangle.

rules.name: The Signal-Is-A-Stroke Rule
rules.body: Signal red is a border, underline, ring, curve or counting numeral. It is a fill only on the primary button and skip link, and then as signal-fill, never as signal.

rules.name: The Mono Number Rule
rules.body: Every measured number, unit, identifier, DOI, list year and readout is set in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals; code, time and data elements inherit it globally. Two exceptions keep a sentence whole: counts in running prose are spelled as words, and a date inside a STIX sentence (the Ph.D. date in About) keeps the sentence's serif. A measured value in Archivo or STIX is a defect.

rules.name: The One Formatter Rule
rules.body: A precision is a property of the quantity, not of the page: kPa at one decimal, FFR at two (three in the metrics table), seconds at two, mm at one, all through lib/format.ts. Two renderings of one value at different precisions on the same surface are a defect.

rules.name: The Even Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings carry one weight (600) and body one weight (400). Rank is carried by size, measure and border ink, never by bolding.

rules.name: The Unit Keeps Its Case Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is chrome for short identifiers (C1, 2026, FLOW, PINO-DEMO-01) and for tags; units and ratios are never uppercased and never tracked.

rules.name: The One Left Edge Rule
rules.body: Every column starts where the frames, nav and footer start. Headings, prose, plates, captions and the Close all sit on that edge; a centered narrower text box, a centered plate or an indented caption breaks it. Measure is the only thing that narrows text.

rules.name: The Hairline-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px line or a tonal step. A box-shadow that leaves a surface is a defect; the only box-shadow in the build is an inset 2px underline on a pressed segmented button, which is an underline by another property, not an elevation.

rules.name: The One Grain Rule
rules.body: Film surfaces carry exactly one grain layer, applied by body::after at 256px tiling and 5% opacity. Nothing else textures a surface.

rules.name: The One Anatomy Rule
rules.body: A paper reads the same on every page (home Led, /research PaperFrame, /publications PubEntry): title (linked to the DOI when one exists), authors, venue line in mono, then the DOI and the role mark on one row. A role mark, tag or corner label never sits directly above a heading at any width; that is the eyebrow the craft floor bans. The same holds for patents (REGISTERED sits beside "Registered No.") and talk rows (tags after the venue, on mobile too). Each /publications entry has one BibTeX control, a disclosure whose panel holds the Copy action and the entry; "Email for a copy" (mailto, subject naming the paper id) sits on the DOI row.

rules.name: The Result-Plate Rule
rules.body: A paper figure earns a plate only when it shows a result (fields, curves, measured errors), never a method flowchart or an architecture diagram: those break the Two-Ink Rule and read as slides. Every plate is captioned in STIX italic naming the figure and the paper (id, journal initials, volume, year), sits on the shared left edge (never centered) as a light-box sheet padded 1rem with a hairline, is capped at 35rem (560px; a wide chart gets 50rem), links to its full-size file with a zoom-in cursor, keeps its caption under the plate's left edge at 62ch, and ships with provenance (a <file>.json sidecar or the manifest's source). Current plates: the phase-scrubber frames and Fig. 9 (J1) on /research#image, and the C1 CFD-against-PINO panel on /publications. Dropped by this rule: the J2 viscosity flowchart and the J4 workflow figure (on /publications and /research), and the 4D CT Fig. 1 architecture in both its white and black-ground versions (the black-ground file also loses its labels and arrows, which are black on black). A J2 visual returns only as its viscosity result panel (predicted against measured), cropped from the paper with provenance.

dos: Do put every data artifact inside a Frame with mono corner chrome and the three-tier stack (what / result / consequence); the frame is the unit of the page.
Do end every page with the shared Close, and keep Email (primary) and CV (PDF) (ghost) one click away in the nav on every page.
Do give a paper the one anatomy everywhere: title, authors, venue, then DOI and role mark on one row.
Do read only the semantic aliases (--bg, --ink, --line, and their tiers) in components so they sit on film and light box unchanged.
Do set every number, unit, identifier and readout in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals, and compute it from the manifest or content data.
Do carry rank by border ink and frame size: signal border for first-author, ink for co-first, hairline for co-author; the larger frame for led work.
Do keep signal red a stroke (border, underline, ring, curve, counting numeral) and reserve signal-fill for the single primary action and the skip link.
Do draw field colors from lib/colormaps.ts only: turbo for pressure, diverging for signed error with the above-range yellow, viridis for speed and spectrograms.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion on every autonomous motion: drift to 0s, develop snapped, transforms removed.

Do format every value through lib/format.ts: kPa at one decimal, FFR at two (three in the metrics table), seconds at two, a narrow no-break space before the unit, doi: lowercase with no space, and one manuscript label, "under revision (EAAI)".
Do start every column on the one left edge and narrow text by measure (60ch prose, 62ch captions), never by a narrower centered box.
Do write the copy that speaks for the owner in the first person (About, the Close, the "my part" lines); third person belongs to author lists and to collaborators' work.
donts: Don't use drop shadows, glows, gradients, blur or translucent panels on any surface; separation is a hairline or a one-step tonal lift.
Don't add kickers, eyebrows or section numbers above headings, including a role mark, tag or label printed directly over a title; the heading carries itself.
Don't plate a method flowchart or architecture figure from a paper; plates are results only, captioned, with provenance.
Don't introduce a second accent or a fourth ink tier; the palette is one ink family per surface plus one red.
Don't uppercase a unit or a ratio (kPa, mm, s, Pd/Pa) or track it; uppercase is for short identifiers in corners and tags only.
Don't fill a role mark or tag; rank is border ink, never a colored chip.
Don't animate the grain, loop the vessel for decoration, or run any motion that is not evidence of a measured quantity.
Don't use icon fonts or glyph characters; icons are inline Phosphor SVGs sized to the text.
Don't print a manuscript's status twice, as a tag, or in another wording; it is one label in one place per entry.
